title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are in a state of flux, with budget discussions heating up and new contracts being awarded. Meanwhile, the race for advanced technology continues, albeit with some hiccups along the way.

themes.title: Budget Battles Heat Up
themes.body: The Space Force's budget is poised for a significant increase, with proposals adding $1.4 billion for resilience efforts. This suggests a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities amid increasing geopolitical tensions.

themes.title: Commercial Data Infrastructure Gains Traction
themes.body: Bluestaq's launch of a defense-grade data infrastructure indicates a shift towards integrating commercial solutions in government operations. This trend could reshape how data is utilized across both sectors, enhancing efficiency and responsiveness.

themes.title: AI Technology in Defense
themes.body: With Slingshot Aerospace securing contracts for AI-enabled training and mission rehearsal, the Defense Department is clearly betting on artificial intelligence to enhance operational readiness. This move reflects a broader trend of integrating advanced technologies into military frameworks.

themes.title: Space Development Agency's Expansion
themes.body: The SDA's latest awards for missile defense tracking satellites underscore a commitment to rapid deployment of space capabilities. However, the persistent delays in hypersonic tests remind us that even the most ambitious plans can face significant hurdles.
